questions.question: What is the prototype chain in JavaScript? How does property lookup work?
questions.title: JavaScript Prototype Chain — How Property Lookup Works
questions.direct_answer:
What is the prototype chain in JavaScript? How does property lookup work?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the type checker, emit pipeline, and how types line up with runtime JS), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Prototype chain traversal for property lookup, Object.prototype at the top, null as the terminator, performance implications.

**Classic weak answer:** Confusing prototype with __proto__ — prototype is a property of constructor functions; __proto__ is the reference each object uses to chain.

**Senior finish:** Discuss property shadowing, performance cost of deep chains, hidden classes in V8, and how Object.create(null) makes a prototype-less object.

interviewer_intent.testing: Prototype chain traversal for property lookup, Object.prototype at the top, null as the terminator, performance implications
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Confusing prototype with __proto__ — prototype is a property of constructor functions; __proto__ is the reference each object uses to chain
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Discuss property shadowing, performance cost of deep chains, hidden classes in V8, and how Object.create(null) makes a prototype-less object

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **JavaScript Prototype Chain — How Property Lookup Works** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** What is the prototype chain in JavaScript? How does property lookup work?

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **Prototype chain traversal for property lookup, Object.prototype at the top, null as the terminator, performance implications**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Confusing prototype with __proto__ — prototype is a property of constructor functions; __proto__ is the reference each object uses to chain**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Discuss property shadowing, performance cost of deep chains, hidden classes in V8, and how Object.create(null) makes a prototype-less object**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** Prototype chain traversal for property lookup, Object.prototype at the top, null as the terminator, performance implications
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

questions.question: What is the difference between __proto__ and prototype in JavaScript?
questions.title: __proto__ vs prototype in JavaScript — Differences Explained
questions.direct_answer:
What is the difference between __proto__ and prototype in JavaScript?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the type checker, emit pipeline, and how types line up with runtime JS), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** __proto__ is the reference every object uses to look up its chain; prototype is a property only on constructor functions used when creating instances.

**Classic weak answer:** Using them interchangeably, or thinking __proto__ is standard (it's legacy; Object.getPrototypeOf is the standard API).

**Senior finish:** Reference the Object.getPrototypeOf / Object.setPrototypeOf standard APIs, and note that __proto__ mutation is slow and deoptimizes engines.

interviewer_intent.testing: __proto__ is the reference every object uses to look up its chain; prototype is a property only on constructor functions used when creating instances
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Using them interchangeably, or thinking __proto__ is standard (it's legacy; Object.getPrototypeOf is the standard API)
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Reference the Object.getPrototypeOf / Object.setPrototypeOf standard APIs, and note that __proto__ mutation is slow and deoptimizes engines

questions.question: How do ES6 classes work under the hood? Are they different from prototypal inheritance?
questions.title: ES6 Class vs Prototypal Inheritance — Syntactic Sugar or More?
questions.direct_answer:
How do ES6 classes work under the hood? Are they different from prototypal inheritance?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the type checker, emit pipeline, and how types line up with runtime JS), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** ES6 classes are syntactic sugar over prototypes; extends + super wire up the prototype chain; differences include hoisting, strict-mode-by-default, non-enumerable methods.

**Classic weak answer:** Thinking classes introduce a new inheritance model — they use the same prototype chain under the hood.

**Senior finish:** Point out real class-only features: private fields #x, static blocks, new.target; and that class methods are non-enumerable by default unlike prototype assignments.

interviewer_intent.testing: ES6 classes are syntactic sugar over prototypes; extends + super wire up the prototype chain; differences include hoisting, strict-mode-by-default, non-enumerable methods
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Thinking classes introduce a new inheritance model — they use the same prototype chain under the hood
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Point out real class-only features: private fields #x, static blocks, new.target; and that class methods are non-enumerable by default unlike prototype assignments
